data.app-logo#App Logo:
The app logo setting allows you to set a home screen logo. It is recommended to use 240x240px PNG images for optimal quality.
Images can be imported and exported from a JSON configuration. A restart may be required for the new image to apply.
data.app-theme#App Theme:
The app theme selector allows you to customize the app’s appearance.
Themes can be imported and exported from a JSON configuration. A restart may be required for the new theme to apply.
data.developer-options#Developer Options: The developer settings menu contains undocumented configuration options that may make the app unusable. Do not change them unless you know what you are doing.
data.device-specific-configuration#Device-Spe:
These configuration options are only available on certain platforms:
Android Lockdown (Android-only)
data.fixed-station#Fixed Station: The fixed station option will disable the location selection. All members will be clocked in from a static location, with no drop-down.
data.importexport#Import/Export:
Configuration exports will contain the service account credentials stored in plain text! Do not share your settings exports. Configurations can be exported as a JSON file, and imported from a JSON file.
The Raspberry Pi Installer will set up USB auto-mount. USB drives are the recommended way for moving configurations.
data.log-level#Log Level: This sets the app’s logging level to be used in the Log Viewer, and terminal output (is running on desktop).
data.oauth-credentials#OAuth Credentials: This step is required. Credentials can be uploaded to the app from a JSON file, provided during the account setup stage. Only importing credentials is supported. It is recommended to use a USB drive storing credentials.
data.require-pin-for-admin-sign-in#Require PI: Require a PIN for manual (non-RFID) admin clock in/out. This setting doesn’t affect RFID operation.
data.reset-pin#Reset PIN:
The reset PIN option will allow you to set a new global PIN. The global PIN is used for accessing configurations, and logs.
The global PIN does not allow for admin clocking in. Those are stored in the Google Sheet.
data.rfid-card-reader-settings#RFID Card Read: This menu allows you to enable or disable an HID card reader. More info can be found here.
data.spreadsheet-id#Spreadsheet ID:
This step is required. This configuration takes in the sheet ID acquired from the sheet creation step.
The service account’s email address must be set as an editor in the sheet’s permission.
data.station-locations#Station Locations:
The station location options allow you to set the location options for clocking in.
You can add, delete, and move location options. The first option is the default when clocking in.

data: It is easy to bypass the Android Lockdown mode to gain unauthorized access to the device. Consider other management options if security is a concern.
data.absorb-volume-keys#Absorb Volume Keys: This will prevent the volume buttons from changing the device volume.
data.default-launcher#Default Launcher:
Second can be set as the default app launcher. This will make it the home screen of the device, preventing users from accessing other apps.
You may use the configuration menu to un-set Second as the default launcher when needed.
data.immersivefullscreen-ui#Immersive/Fullscr: This will hide the system navigation and status bars, and run the app in fullscreen mode.

data.can-a-physical-keyboard-be-used-with-the: No, a physical keyboard will not work with the app, even if RFID is disabled. The app will only work using the virtual keyboard. This also applies to desktop platforms.

data.how-do-i-reset-the-password-of-an-admin-: Delete the member’s “Password Hash” from the Members workbook within the Google Sheet. The member will be prompted to set a new PIN the next time they try to clock in/out.
data.what-timestamp-format-is-used-in-the-goo: Timestamps are recorded in the --T::.Z format. All timestamps are recorded using UTC.
data.whats-the-difference-between-an-admin-me: Admin members are configured by default to require a PIN for manual (non-RFID) clock in/out, while student members do not require a PIN.
data.whats-the-difference-between-the-global-:
The global admin PIN is used to access the app’s configuration settings and logs. It is a universal PIN that allows authorized users to manage the app’s settings.
An admin member’s PIN, on the other hand, is specific to individual admin members stored in the Google Sheet. This PIN is used for clocking in and out if the admin does not use RFID.

data:
Set up the Google Cloud project, service account, and sheet that Second uses to store member lists and activity logs.
Service AccountCreate a Google Cloud project, enable the Google Sheets API, and download the service account credentials. Template SheetCopy the template sheet, and add your members and kiosk locations.

Second uses a Google Sheet for member lists, status tracking, and log keeping. Second requires a Service Account to authenticate with Google. This guide will walk you through the steps for setting up a service account with access to the Google Sheets API.
You must have the ability to use the Google Cloud Console within your organization. (Only applicable if you are in an organization account)
data.adding-the-google-sheets-api#Adding the:
Click “View all APIs”
Search and Select “Google Sheets API”
Click “Enable” under the API
data.creating-a-google-cloud-project#Creating:
For the Attendance Tracker to be able to talk to Google then the Google Sheet needs to be associated with a Google Project.
To create a project go to https://console.cloud.google.com/projectselector2/ .
Click “Create Project”
On the next window, for the Project Name use “Attendance Tracking”.
Click “Create”.
Next you should see a “welcome” screen and indicate “You’re working in Attendance Tracking”.
data.creating-the-json-credentials-for-second:
Now we need to download the credentials we just created so click the “Credentials” tab in the middle of the window (NOT the Create Credentials we clicked earlier).
Select your service account’s email.
Go to the “Keys” tab.
Select “Create new key” under the “Add key” drop-down.
Create a “JSON” private key.
Once you click create, a JSON credential file will be downloaded. Save this file on to a USB drive that you can plug into your kiosk.
This file contains the authentication keys for the service account. Store it securely.
data.creating-the-service-account#Creating th:
Once the API is enabled, you should be redirected to the “APIs & Services” page. Click “Create Credentials”.
Select “Application Data” and continue.
Create your service account. Add a name, ID, and description.
It is highly recommended to create separate accounts for each kiosk you may be using. Name them something unique. Note down this email address, it will be used when we create the Template Sheet On the next screen in the “Select a role” dropdown type “editor” then select the Editor entry from the drop-down list then click “continue”, then finally “Done”.
Click “Continue”.
Skip the “Principals with access” section, and click “Done”.
data.next-steps#Next Steps:
Now that you have your credentials file, it can be imported into Second.
Create the sheet that Second will use.

data:
A template Google Sheet for Second is provided here . Make a copy of it.
Make the service account’s email an editor of your copy. The app will not work if it doesn’t have access to the sheet.
data.adding-more-members#Adding more members:
More members can be added by duplicating existing member rows and changing their attributes. By default, it may take up to 90 seconds before new members are populated in the kiosks.
Ensure that each member’s ID is unique. Second is not able to handle duplicate IDs, and will behave unexpectedly.
data.getting-the-sheets-id#Getting the Sheet’:
The sheet ID can be retrieved from the URL of your copy.
For example the ID of https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1oSpvY5a2ia-BMnCmbfHnVarhzfLuNhgHjvAtxOJZANI/edit?gid=2019486561#gid=2019486561
Is: 1oSpvY5a2ia-BMnCmbfHnVarhzfLuNhgHjvAtxOJZANI
data.log-sheet#Log Sheet:
The log sheet contains a list of each member’s sign in and out activity. Kiosks that are authenticated into the sheet will add new lines to this sheet every time someone clocks in or out. Timestamps and clock in location (if clocking in) will be recorded here.
Do not manually modify the sheet’s header (row 2). The app may not function correctly if anything is changed.
data.members-sheet#Members Sheet:
This sheet contains each member’s unique ID, name, role (admin or student), presence, location, and password hash (only used for admins).
The template above includes examples for admin and student accounts
data.resetting-an-admins-pin#Resetting an Adm: Simply clear the password hash from the sheet. The admin will be asked to create a new PIN on the kiosk the next time they sign in.
data.what-is-the-password-hash#What is the Pa: The password hash is a SHA256 hash of the admin’s password.

data:
Second supports a Raspberry Pi 5 running Pi OS Bookworm or newer. It may be possible to use it on a Pi 4 or older, but this is untested.
An automated installation script is provided to simplify the setup process of a kiosk system.
The kiosk installation requires Pi OS Lite. Running the installation script on a full Pi OS installation will NOT WORK.
data.booting-the-pi#Booting the Pi:
Insert the flashed microSD card into the Raspberry Pi and power it on. If using Ethernet, connect the network cable before powering on.
Upon booting the Pi, you will see a “My IP address is …” message. Take note of the IP address for SSH access.
data.connect-to-the-pi-via-ssh#Connect to the:
SSH is available on all Macs, Linux systems, and Windows 10 or newer.
You can use your computer’s Terminal (Mac, Linux) or Command Prompt (Windows) app to use SSH.
Run the following command, replacing username with the username you set during the Pi OS Lite installation, and ip_address with the IP address displayed on the Pi:
ssh username@ip_address You will be asked to accept the Pi’s SSH key and enter the password you set during installation.
Once in the Pi’s shell, you are ready to complete the next steps.
data.flashing-sd-card-with-pi-os-lite#Flashin:
Raspberry Pi Imager is required to flash the microSD card. This guide is written for Pi Imager 2.0.0 or newer.
Select the target board
Select Pi OS Lite (64-bit)
Raspberry Pi OS (other) → Raspberry Pi OS Lite (64-bit)
Select the microSD card
Insert the microSD card into your computer and select it in Pi Imager.
This will erase all data on the selected drive. Customization
Here you will enable SSH and set up Wi-Fi (if not using Ethernet or your kiosk).
Hostname
Configure a unique hostname for your Raspberry Pi.
Localization
Set your locale, timezone, and keyboard layout.
User
Set a username and password for the kiosk’s user (the kiosk will auto-login).
Wi-Fi
Configure your Wi-Fi SSID and password. Leave the fields blank if using Ethernet.
Remote access
Enable SSH to allow remote access to the Raspberry Pi for running the installation script.
Raspberry Pi Connect
Skip this step. Raspberry Pi Connect will not work with the kiosk setup.
Write the image
Before writing, double-check all settings.
Press Write and for the image to be flashed and verified.
data.post-installation#Post-Installation:
Congratulations! Your Raspberry Pi should now boot directly into the Second kiosk application.
Configure the device by following the guide here.
data.requirements#Requirements: Raspberry Pi 5 microSD card (8GB or larger) Another computer to flash the microSD card Internet connection Keyboard and mouse (for initial setup) Display (touchscreen recommended for kiosk use)
data.running-the-kiosk-installer#Running the:
Python’s Virtual Environment module is required to run the installation script.
Install it with:
sudo apt install python3-venv Download the installation script:
curl -SLo install.py https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MercsMavs-MSA/Second/refs/heads/main/pi_os_installer/main.py Run the installation script with superuser privileges:
The installation process may take a while (~10-20 minutes). sudo python3 install.py Reboot the Pi into the new kiosk environment:
sudo reboot

data:
Reference for the screens and controls in the Second kiosk app.
Home ScreenThe member list, virtual keyboard, search bar, connection status, and menu. Member PageClock in and out, select a location, and view member details.

data.1-members-list#1. Members List: The members list contains a list of all currently registered members from the Members Sheet
data.2-virtual-keyboard#2. Virtual Keyboard: The virtual keyboard is the ONLY way to type into the search bar. A physical keyboard is not supported, even if RFID is disabled.
data.3-manual-members-refresh-button#3. Manua: The manual members refresh button will schedule a re-pull of the members list from the Google Sheet. It will bypass the app’s regular timed event scheduling loop.
data.4-member-search-bar#4. Member Search Bar: The member search bar is visual-only. It does not have to be focused to type with the virtual keyboard.
data.5-date-and-time#5. Date and Time: Date and time representative of the timestamps to be placed in the activity log.
data.6-organization-logo-configurable#6. Orga: The organization logo is customizable through the app’s configuration. It is recommended to use a 240x240 PNG image for best results.
data.7-google-sheet-connection-status#7. Goog:
The connection status card will show the current status of the Google Sheets backend.
It will say “System Online” if the app is connected to the sheet.
“Connection Lost” will be displayed if any of the following are true:
No Internet Connection Backend is being Rate-Limited Sheet ID is incorrect Service Account is not authorized or not set up
data.8-menu#8. Menu: The menu contains items for managing the app’s configuration, and viewing error logs (both require the global admin PIN to access).

data:
The member page can be accessed by selecting your name from the list, or by scanning in your RFID badge.
Admin members may require a PIN code, if configured. If the admin hasn’t created a PIN yet, they will be requested to do so within the app.
data.1-clock-in-button#1. Clock In Button: The clock in button will clock the member in. The timestamp and selected location will be recorded in the activity log.
data.2-clock-out-button#2. Clock Out Button: The clock out button will clock out the member. The timestamp only will be recorded in the activity log.
data.3-location-selection#3. Location Selecti: The location selector will select the location to clock in to. It will not be visible if the member is currently clocked in. The locations can be configured in the app’s configuration.
data.4-member-profile-image#4. Member Profile: The profile image currently only displays the member’s initials. Image support may be added in the future.
data.5-member-id#5. Member ID: The member ID is the unique identifier used in the sheet. The RFID tag’s UID must match this for it to work.
